nodes.label: Standing
nodes.description: The subject is up on both feet and not moving anywhere, which is the plainest and most neutral body position there is.
examples: a person standing still in the middle of a room
full-length portrait of someone standing on a pavement

nodes.label: Contrapposto stance
nodes.description: A relaxed standing position where the weight rests on one leg so that one hip lifts and the shoulders tilt the other way, giving the body a gentle S-curve. It is the pose you see in classical statues and in most fashion photography.
examples: model standing with the weight on the back leg and one hip pushed out
relaxed standing portrait with a soft S-curve through the body
nodes.prompt_fragment: standing in contrapposto with the weight on one leg

nodes.label: Wide stance
nodes.description: Standing with the feet planted well apart, which reads as confident, grounded or defiant rather than relaxed.
examples: figure standing with feet planted wide on a rooftop
athlete braced with legs apart before a start
nodes.prompt_fragment: standing with feet planted wide apart
nodes.negative_fragment: not standing with a wide stance

nodes.label: Leaning
nodes.description: The subject rests part of their weight on something else, such as a wall, a railing or a car, instead of carrying it on their own legs.
examples: person leaning on a balcony railing
figure propped against a parked car

nodes.label: Leaning against a wall
nodes.description: The subject stands with their back or shoulder pressed against a wall, a very common street-portrait pose that flattens the body against the background.
examples: shoulder against a painted brick wall, one foot up behind
back flat to a concrete wall in an alley

nodes.label: Walking pose
nodes.description: The body is shaped as if walking, with one leg ahead of the other, whether or not the person is really travelling. Use this when you want the shape of a walk; use the action Walking when you want the activity itself.
examples: one foot forward, arms swinging slightly, frozen in a walk
runway-style walking posture

nodes.label: Mid-stride
nodes.description: The exact moment of a step where the legs are furthest apart and one foot has left the ground, which makes a still photograph feel like it has movement in it.
examples: rear foot lifting off a wet pavement
street shot frozen at the widest point of a step

nodes.label: Sitting
nodes.description: The subject rests on their bottom with the upper body upright, on a chair, a step, a bed or the ground.
examples: seated on a wooden chair by a window
sitting on the edge of a bed

nodes.label: Sitting cross-legged
nodes.description: Sitting with the legs folded in front of the body and each ankle tucked under the opposite knee, the way people sit on the floor or on a bed.
examples: sitting cross-legged on a rug
cross-legged on a bed with a book

nodes.label: Seated on the floor
nodes.description: Sitting directly on the ground or floor rather than on furniture, which lowers the whole subject inside the frame.
examples: sitting on a kerb with legs stretched out
seated on a studio floor against a plain wall

nodes.label: Perched on an edge
aliases: balanced on the edge of a table
nodes.description: Sitting lightly on the edge of something high, such as a ledge, a desk or a stool, with the feet often still touching the ground.
examples: perched on the edge of a desk
sitting on a rooftop ledge with legs hanging over
nodes.prompt_fragment: perched on the edge of a surface

nodes.label: Crouching
nodes.description: The knees are bent deeply so the body drops close to the ground while the feet stay flat and the weight stays on the legs.
examples: crouched beside a bicycle wheel
photographer crouching low on a street corner

nodes.label: Squatting
nodes.description: A very low crouch where the backs of the thighs rest on the calves and the hips almost touch the heels, a comfortable resting position rather than a momentary duck.
examples: squatting on a kerb waiting for a bus
resting in a deep squat against a shopfront

nodes.label: Kneeling
nodes.description: The subject rests on their knees on the ground with the lower legs folded back underneath them.
examples: kneeling on a studio floor
kneeling in grass to tie a shoelace

nodes.label: Kneeling on one knee
nodes.description: Only one knee touches the ground while the other leg stays bent in front, a stable half-kneeling position used in sport, proposals and hero shots.
examples: down on one knee at the edge of a pitch
half-kneeling beside a dog

nodes.label: Lying down
nodes.description: The whole body is horizontal, resting on a bed, a floor, grass or any flat surface.
examples: lying flat on a bed shot from above
stretched out on grass in a park

nodes.label: Lying on the back
nodes.description: Lying face up, so the face and the front of the body are turned towards the sky or the ceiling.
examples: lying face up on a wooden floor
on their back in long grass looking at the sky
nodes.prompt_fragment: lying on their back, face up

nodes.label: Lying on the side
nodes.description: Lying horizontally but turned onto one shoulder and hip, often with the knees drawn up.
examples: curled on one side on a sofa
lying sideways across a bed, head propped on a hand

nodes.label: Lying on the stomach
nodes.description: Lying face down with the chest towards the ground, often with the upper body propped on the elbows.
examples: lying face down on a bed, chin on hands
propped on elbows on a picnic blanket

nodes.label: Reclining
nodes.description: A relaxed position halfway between sitting and lying, with the upper body angled back and supported by cushions, elbows or a headboard.
examples: reclining on a sofa with one arm along the back
propped up on elbows on a beach towel

nodes.label: Bending forward
nodes.description: The upper body folds forward at the waist while the legs stay more or less straight, as when reaching for something on the ground.
examples: bending forward to pick up a bag
bowed forward over a workbench

nodes.label: Arms crossed
nodes.description: Both arms are folded across the chest. This is an arm detail that can sit on top of any main pose, so it never fights with standing, sitting or leaning.
examples: standing with arms folded across the chest
seated portrait with crossed arms

nodes.label: Hands in pockets
nodes.description: Both hands are pushed into trouser or jacket pockets, a relaxed and casual arm detail that layers on top of any main pose.
examples: walking with both hands buried in coat pockets
leaning on a wall, hands in jeans pockets

nodes.label: Hand on hip
nodes.description: One hand rests on the hip with the elbow pushed out to the side, a classic confident fashion detail that pairs naturally with a weight-on-one-leg stance.
examples: standing with one hand on the hip, elbow out
editorial pose with hand resting on the waist
nodes.prompt_fragment: one hand resting on the hip

nodes.label: Hands behind the back
nodes.description: Both hands are held out of sight behind the body, which reads as formal, patient or reserved.
examples: standing straight with hands clasped behind the back
waiting with arms tucked behind the body

nodes.label: Hands clasped in front
nodes.description: The hands are held together in front of the body, fingers interlocked or one hand cupping the other, a quiet and slightly formal detail.
examples: seated with hands folded in the lap
standing with fingers interlocked in front
nodes.prompt_fragment: hands clasped in front of the body

nodes.label: Arms raised
nodes.description: Both arms are lifted above shoulder height, which opens up the silhouette and usually reads as celebration, stretching or surrender.
examples: both arms thrown up above the head
hands lifted overhead against a bright sky

nodes.label: Arms at the sides
nodes.description: The arms simply hang down beside the body with nothing held and nothing crossed, the most neutral possible arm position.
examples: standing straight with arms hanging loosely
plain full-length portrait, arms relaxed at the sides
nodes.prompt_fragment: arms hanging relaxed at the sides
nodes.negative_fragment: arms not hanging at the sides

nodes.label: Legs crossed
nodes.description: One leg is placed over or in front of the other, either while seated on a chair or while standing with the ankles crossed. It is a leg detail that layers on top of the main pose.
examples: seated with one knee crossed over the other
standing against a wall with ankles crossed

nodes.label: Head tilted
nodes.description: The head leans towards one shoulder instead of sitting straight, a small detail that softens a portrait and adds curiosity or playfulness.
examples: head tilted slightly towards the left shoulder
portrait with a soft head tilt and a small smile

nodes.label: Body turned three-quarters
nodes.description: The body is rotated part way between facing the camera and facing sideways, so one shoulder is nearer than the other. It slims the silhouette and is the default body angle in most portraits.
examples: shoulders angled about forty-five degrees to the lens
body turned away while the face returns to camera
nodes.prompt_fragment: body turned three-quarters to the camera

nodes.label: Back to camera
nodes.description: The subject is turned away so the camera sees their back and the face is hidden, which puts all the attention on the outfit, the hair and the scene ahead of them.
examples: figure walking away, seen from behind
back turned to the lens on a beach at sunset
nodes.prompt_fragment: seen from behind with the back to the camera
nodes.negative_fragment: not turned away from the camera

nodes.label: Looking at the camera
nodes.description: The subject's eyes meet the lens, so the finished picture feels like the person is looking straight at whoever is viewing it.
examples: direct eye contact with the lens
portrait staring calmly into the camera

nodes.label: Looking away
nodes.description: The eyes are directed somewhere outside the frame instead of at the lens, which makes the picture feel observed rather than posed.
examples: gaze drifting past the camera to the left
looking out of a window, away from the lens
nodes.negative_fragment: not looking away from the camera

nodes.label: Glancing over the shoulder
nodes.description: The body faces away while the head turns back, so the face appears past one shoulder. Do not confuse it with an over-the-shoulder shot, which describes where the camera is rather than what the subject does.
examples: walking away and glancing back at the lens
head turned back over the left shoulder

nodes.label: Looking down
nodes.description: The eyes and usually the chin are lowered towards the ground, which reads as thoughtful, shy or private.
examples: eyes lowered towards the hands
chin down, gaze on the pavement

nodes.label: Looking up
nodes.description: The chin lifts and the eyes point above the horizon, which reads as hopeful, awed or searching.
examples: chin raised, eyes towards the sky
looking up at tall buildings

nodes.label: Slouched posture
nodes.description: The spine curves and the shoulders roll forward instead of being held straight, which reads as tired, casual or unguarded.
examples: slumped in a chair with rounded shoulders
slouching against a bus stop

nodes.label: Upright posture
nodes.description: The spine is held straight and the shoulders are open and level, which reads as poised, formal or self-assured.
examples: standing tall with shoulders squared
seated with a straight back and lifted chest

nodes.label: Candid, unposed
nodes.description: The body is doing something ordinary rather than holding a pose for the camera, so the picture feels caught rather than arranged.
examples: caught mid-conversation without noticing the camera
unposed street moment

nodes.label: Deliberately posed
nodes.description: The subject is knowingly holding a position for the photograph, the way a model holds a shape in a studio or an editorial shoot.
examples: holding a deliberate editorial shape in a studio
posing consciously for a fashion frame

nodes.label: Walking
nodes.description: The subject is travelling on foot at an ordinary pace. Use this for the activity itself; use the Walking pose when you only want the shape of a step in a still frame.
examples: walking along a wet pavement at night
crossing a street with shopping bags

nodes.label: Running
nodes.description: The subject is moving quickly on foot with both feet leaving the ground between steps.
examples: running across a park at dusk
running down a corridor, hair flying back

nodes.label: Sprinting
nodes.description: Running at absolute top speed with the body pitched forward and the arms driving hard, as in a race rather than a jog.
examples: sprinting off a starting line
flat-out run down an empty road

nodes.label: Crawling
nodes.description: Moving forward on the hands and knees, close to the ground.
examples: crawling under a low fence
child crawling across a carpet

nodes.label: Climbing
nodes.description: Moving upward using both hands and feet, on stairs, a ladder, a rock face or a fence.
examples: climbing a fire escape
scaling a boulder with both hands on the rock

nodes.label: Swimming
nodes.description: Moving through water using the arms and legs.
examples: swimming lengths in a lit pool
swimming out through calm sea water

nodes.label: Dancing
nodes.description: Moving the body rhythmically to music, whether that is a formal step or a loose improvisation.
examples: dancing alone in a kitchen
dancing in a crowd under coloured lights

nodes.label: Riding
nodes.description: Travelling while sitting on or astride something that carries you, such as a bike, a motorbike, a horse or a scooter.
examples: riding along a coastal road
riding a horse through a field

nodes.label: Riding a bicycle
nodes.description: Travelling by bicycle, with the hands on the bars and the feet on the pedals.
examples: cycling through a city bike lane
riding a bike along a canal path

nodes.label: Riding a motorcycle
nodes.description: Travelling astride a motorcycle, motorbike or scooter.
examples: riding a motorbike down a night highway
sitting astride a scooter pulling away from a kerb

nodes.label: Skateboarding
aliases: doing a trick on a board
nodes.description: Riding a skateboard, whether cruising along or in the middle of a trick.
examples: skating along an empty car park
mid-trick with the board off the ground

nodes.label: Sitting down
nodes.description: The movement of lowering the body into a seat. This is the act of sitting down, not the settled Sitting pose that follows it.
examples: lowering into a cafe chair
about to drop onto a sofa

nodes.label: Standing up
nodes.description: The movement of rising from a seated or crouched position onto the feet.
examples: pushing up out of an armchair
rising from a park bench

nodes.label: Jumping
nodes.description: Pushing off the ground so the whole body is briefly in the air.
examples: leaping off a low wall
caught mid-air above a puddle

nodes.label: Turning
nodes.description: Rotating the body or the head to face a new direction, often caught halfway through the turn.
examples: turning sharply towards a sound
spinning round so the coat flares out

nodes.label: Reaching
nodes.description: Extending an arm towards something, whether or not the hand has arrived yet.
examples: reaching for a book on a high shelf
hand extended towards a shop window

nodes.label: Stretching
nodes.description: Extending the limbs or arching the body to lengthen the muscles, as when waking up or warming up.
examples: stretching both arms overhead by a window
runner stretching against a railing

nodes.label: Waving
nodes.description: Lifting a hand and moving it side to side as a greeting or a farewell.
examples: waving from a train window
raised hand waving across a street

nodes.label: Pointing
nodes.description: Extending a finger or a whole hand to indicate something, usually while looking the same way.
examples: pointing at something off to the left
guide pointing up at a building

nodes.label: Throwing
nodes.description: Launching an object away from the body with the arm.
examples: throwing a ball across a beach
tossing a jacket over one shoulder

nodes.label: Holding an object
nodes.description: The subject has something in their hand, whatever that object happens to be. Name the object itself with a Props value.
examples: holding a paper cup in one hand
gripping a camera at chest height
nodes.prompt_fragment: holding an object in one hand

nodes.label: Carrying a bag
nodes.description: The subject is carrying a bag, a case or shopping, in the hand or slung over a shoulder.
examples: walking with two paper shopping bags
tote bag hanging from one shoulder

nodes.label: Adjusting hair
nodes.description: A hand goes up to the hair to push it back, tuck it behind an ear or hold it out of the face, a small everyday gesture that reads as natural and unstaged.
examples: tucking hair behind one ear
pushing wind-blown hair off the face
nodes.prompt_fragment: adjusting their hair with one hand

nodes.label: Adjusting clothing
nodes.description: The hands are busy with what the subject is wearing, straightening a collar, buttoning a coat or pulling a sleeve into place.
examples: straightening a jacket collar
buttoning a coat against the wind

nodes.label: Applying makeup
nodes.description: The subject is putting on makeup, usually in front of a mirror or a phone camera.
examples: applying lipstick in a bathroom mirror
makeup being finished backstage

nodes.label: Opening a door
nodes.description: A hand is on a door, pushing or pulling it open, often at the moment of entering or leaving.
examples: pushing open a glass shop door
hand on a car door about to step out

nodes.label: Checking a phone
nodes.description: The subject is looking at a phone held in the hand, reading, scrolling or typing on it.
examples: scrolling a phone while waiting at a bus stop
face lit by a phone screen at night

nodes.label: Talking
nodes.description: The subject is speaking, usually caught mid-sentence with the mouth open and the hands gesturing.
examples: mid-sentence across a cafe table
talking animatedly with both hands moving

nodes.label: Talking on the phone
nodes.description: The subject holds a phone to the ear and speaks into it.
examples: phone pressed to the ear on a busy street
taking a call while walking
nodes.prompt_fragment: talking on a phone held to the ear

nodes.label: Laughing
nodes.description: The subject is laughing out loud, often with the head tipped back and the eyes creased.
examples: laughing with the head thrown back
caught mid-laugh across a table

nodes.label: Smiling
nodes.description: The mouth curves into a smile, from a faint half-smile to a broad grin.
examples: a small smile towards the lens
broad grin in bright daylight

nodes.label: Reading
nodes.description: The subject is reading something in front of them, a book, a paper or a screen.
examples: reading a paperback on a train
reading a newspaper at a cafe table

nodes.label: Writing
nodes.description: The subject is writing or drawing by hand with a pen or pencil.
examples: writing in a notebook by a window
taking notes at a desk

nodes.label: Typing on a laptop
nodes.description: The hands are on a keyboard, typing at a laptop or a computer.
examples: typing at a laptop in a cafe
hands on a keyboard lit by a screen

nodes.label: Eating
nodes.description: The subject is eating food, whether at a table or on the move.
examples: eating noodles at a counter
biting into a pastry on a bench

nodes.label: Drinking
nodes.description: The subject is drinking from a cup, a glass or a bottle, or lifting one towards the mouth.
examples: sipping coffee from a paper cup
raising a glass at a table

nodes.label: Cooking
nodes.description: The subject is preparing food, chopping, stirring or working at a stove.
examples: chopping vegetables on a wooden board
stirring a pan at a gas hob

nodes.label: Playing an instrument
nodes.description: The subject is playing a musical instrument such as a guitar, a piano or a violin.
examples: strumming a guitar on a bed
hands on piano keys in a dim room

nodes.label: Hugging
nodes.description: Two people hold each other with their arms, in a greeting, a goodbye or a moment of comfort.
examples: two friends hugging on a station platform
arms wrapped around each other in a doorway
